[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.18] (2) The claim form will be deemed to be served unless the address for the defendant on the claim form is not the relevant address for the purpose of rules 6.7 to 6.10. ## Notice of non-service by bailiff

## 6.19 Where –

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.19 Where –] (a) the court bailiff is to serve a claim form; and

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.19 Where –] (b) the bailiff is unable to serve it on the defendant,

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.19 Where –] the court will send notification to the claimant. ## III SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS OTHER THAN THE CLAIM FORM IN THE UNITED KINGDOM

## Methods of service

## 6.20

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.20] (1) A document may be served by any of the following methods –

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.20] (a) personal service, in accordance with rule 6.22;

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.20] (b) first class post, document exchange or other service which provides for delivery on the next business day, in accordance with Practice Direction 6A;

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.20] (c) leaving it at a place specified in rule 6.23;

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.20] (d) fax or other means of electronic communication in accordance with Practice Direction 6A; or

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.20] (e) any method authorised by the court under rule 6.27. [PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.20] (2) A company may be served –

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.20] (a) by any method permitted under this Part; or

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.20] (b) by any of the methods of service permitted under the Companies Act 2006. [PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.20] (3) A limited liability partnership may be served –

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.20] (a) by any method permitted under this Part; or

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.20] (b) by any of the methods of service permitted under the Companies Act 2006 as applied with modification by regulations made under the Limited Liability Partnerships Act 2000. ## Who is to serve

## 6.21

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.21] (1) A party to proceedings will serve a document which that party has prepared except where –

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.21] (a) a rule or practice direction provides that the court will serve the document; or

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.21] (b) the court orders otherwise. [PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.21] (2) The court will serve a document which it has prepared except where –

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.21] (a) a rule or practice direction provides that a party must serve the document;

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.21] (b) the party on whose behalf the document is to be served notifies the court that the party wishes to serve it; or

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.21] (c) the court orders otherwise. [PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.21] (3) Where the court is to serve a document, it is for the court to decide which method of service is to be used. [PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.21] (4) Where the court is to serve a document prepared by a party, that party must provide a copy for the court and for each party to be served. ## Personal service

## 6.22

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.22] (1) Where required by another Part, any other enactment, a practice direction or a court order, a document must be served personally. [PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.22] (2) In other cases, a document may be served personally except –

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.22] (a) where the party to be served has given an address for service under rule 6.23; or

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.22] (b) in any proceedings by or against the Crown. [PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.22] (3) A document may be served personally as if the document were a claim form in accordance with rule 6.5(3). [PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.22] (For service out of the jurisdiction see rules 6.40 to 6.47.)

## Address for service to be given after proceedings are started

## 6.23

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.23] (1) Unless the court orders otherwise, a party to proceedings must give an address at which that party may be served with documents relating to those proceedings. The address must include a full postcode. [PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.23] (2) Except where any other rule, practice direction or order makes different provision, a party’s address for service must be –

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.23] (a) the business address within the United Kingdom of a solicitor acting for the party to be served; or

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.23] (b) Omitted

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.23] (c) where there is no solicitor acting for the party –

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.23] (i) an address within the United Kingdom at which the party resides or carries on business;

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.23] (For Production Centre Claims see paragraph 2.3(7) and (7A) of Practice Direction 7B; for Money Claims Online see paragraph 4(3A) and (6) of Practice Direction 7C; and for Possession Claims Online see paragraph 5.1(3A) and (4) of Practice Direction 55B.)

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.23] (3) Where none of sub-paragraphs (2)(a) or (c) applies unless the court orders otherwise, the party must give an address for service within the United Kingdom. [PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.23] (Part 42 contains provisions about change of solicitor. Rule 42.1 provides that where a party gives the business address of a solicitor as that party’s address for service, that solicitor will be considered to be acting for the party until the provisions of Part 42 are complied with.)

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.23] (4) Subject to the provisions of Section IV of this Part (where applicable), any document to be served in proceedings must be sent or transmitted to, or left at, the party’s address for service under paragraph (2) or (3) unless it is to be served personally or the court orders otherwise. [PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.23] (5) Where, in accordance with Practice Direction 6A, a party indicates or is deemed to have indicated that they will accept service by fax, the fax number given by that party must be at the address for service. [PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.23] (6) Where a party indicates in accordance with Practice Direction 6A that they will accept service by electronic means other than fax, the e-mail address or electronic identification given by that party will be deemed to be at the address for service. [PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.23] (7) In proceedings by or against the Crown, service of any document in the proceedings on the Crown must be effected in the same manner prescribed in rule 6.10 as if the document were a claim form. [PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.23] (8) This rule does not apply where an order made by the court under rule 6.27 (service by an alternative method or at an alternative place) specifies where a document may be served. [PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.23] (For service out of the jurisdiction see rules 6.40 to 6.47.)

## Change of address for service

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > Change of address for service] 6.24 Where the address for service of a party changes, that party must give notice in writing of the change as soon as it has taken place to the court and every other party. ## Service on children and protected parties

## 6.25

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.25] (1) An application for an order appointing a litigation friend where a child or protected party has no litigation friend must be served in accordance with rule 21.8(1) and (2). [PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.25] (2) Any other document which would otherwise be served on a child or a protected party must be served on the litigation friend conducting the proceedings on behalf of the child or protected party. [PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.25] (3) The court may make an order permitting a document to be served on the child or protected party or on some person other than the person specified in rule 21.8 or paragraph (2). [PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.25] (4) An application for an order under paragraph (3) may be made without notice. [PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.25] (5) The court may order that, although a document has been sent or given to someone other than the person specified in rule 21.8 or paragraph (2), the document is to be treated as if it had been properly served. [PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.25] (6) This rule does not apply where the court has made an order under rule 21.2(3) allowing a child to conduct proceedings without a litigation friend. ## Deemed Service

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > Deemed Service] 6.26 A document, other than a claim form, served within the United Kingdom in accordance with these Rules or any relevant practice direction is deemed to be served on the day shown in the following table –

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > Deemed Service] Method of service | Deemed date of service

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > Deemed Service] 1. First class post (or other service which provides for delivery on the next business day) | The second day after it was posted, left with, delivered to or collected by the relevant service provider provided that day is a business day; or if not, the next business day after that day. [PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > Deemed Service] 2. Document exchange | The second day after it was left with, delivered to or collected by the relevant service provider provided that day is a business day; or if not, the next business day after that day. [PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > Deemed Service] 3. Delivering the document to or leaving it at a permitted address | If it is delivered to or left at the permitted address on a business day before 4.30p.m., on that day; or in any other case, on the next business day after that day. [PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > Deemed Service] 4. Fax | If the transmission of the fax is completed on a business day before 4.30p.m., on that day; or in any other case, on the next business day after the day on which it was transmitted. [PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > Deemed Service] 5. Other electronic method | If the e-mail or other electronic transmission is sent on a business day before 4.30p.m., on that day; or in any other case, on the next business day after the day on which it was sent. [PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > Deemed Service] 6. Personal service | If the document is served personally before 4.30p.m. on a business day, on that day; or in any other case, on the next business day after that day. [PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > Deemed Service] (Paragraphs 10.1 to 10.7 of Practice Direction 6A contain examples of how the date of deemed service is calculated.)

## Service by an alternative method or at an alternative place

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > Service by an alternative method or at an alternative place] 6.27 Rule 6.15 applies to any document in the proceedings as it applies to a claim form and reference to the defendant in that rule is modified accordingly. ## Power to dispense with service

## 6.28

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.28] (1) The court may dispense with service of any document which is to be served in the proceedings. [PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.28] (2) An application for an order to dispense with service must be supported by evidence and may be made without notice. ## Certificate of service

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > Certificate of service] 6.29 Where a rule, practice direction or court order requires a certificate of service, the certificate must state the details required by the following table –

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > Certificate of service] Method of Service | Details to be certified

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > Certificate of service] 1. Personal service | Date and time of personal service. [PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > Certificate of service] 2. First class post, document exchange or other service which provides for delivery on the next business day | Date of posting, or leaving with, delivering to or collection by the relevant service provider. [PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > Certificate of service] 3. Delivery of document to or leaving it at a permitted place | Date and time of when the document was delivered to or left at the permitted place. [PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > Certificate of service] 4. Fax | Date and time of completion of the transmission. [PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > Certificate of service] 5. Other electronic method | Date and time of sending the e-mail or other electronic transmission. [PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > Certificate of service] 6. Alternative method or place permitted by the court | As required by the court. ## IV SERVICE OF THE CLAIM FORM AND OTHER DOCUMENTS OUT OF THE JURISDICTION

## Scope of this Section

## 6.30 This Section contains rules about –

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.30 This Section contains rules about –] (a) service of the claim form and other documents out of the jurisdiction;

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.30 This Section contains rules about –] (b) when the permission of the court is required and how to obtain that permission; and

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.30 This Section contains rules about –] (c) the procedure for service. [PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.30 This Section contains rules about –] (‘Jurisdiction’ is defined in rule 2.3(1).)

## Interpretation

## 6.31

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.31] (1) For the purposes of this Section –

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.31] (a) ‘the Hague Convention’ means the Convention on the service abroad of judicial and extrajudicial documents in civil or commercial matters signed at the Hague on 15 November 1965 7 ;

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.31] (b) ‘the 1982 Act’ means the Civil Jurisdiction and Judgments Act 1982 8 ;

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.31] (c) ‘Civil Procedure Convention’ means any and any other Convention (including the Hague Convention) entered into by the United Kingdom regarding service out of the jurisdiction;

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.31] (d) Omitted

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.31] (e) Omitted

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.31] (f) ‘Commonwealth State’ means a state listed in Schedule 3 to the British Nationality Act 1981 14 ;

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.31] (g) Omitted

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.31] (h) Omitted

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.31] (j) Omitted

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.31] (k) ‘the 2005 Hague Convention’ means the Convention on Choice of Court Agreements concluded on 30th June 2005 at the Hague. ## 6.32

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.32] (1) The claimant may serve the claim form on a defendant in Scotland or Northern Ireland where each claim made against the defendant to be served and included in the claim form is a claim which the court has power to determine under the 1982 Act and –

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.32] (a) no proceedings between the parties concerning the same claim are pending in the courts of any other part of the United Kingdom; and

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.32] (b)

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.32] (i) the defendant is domiciled in the United Kingdom;

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.32] (ii) the proceedings are within paragraph 11 of Schedule 4 to the 1982 Act; or

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.32] (iii) the defendant is a party to an agreement conferring jurisdiction, within paragraph 12 of Schedule 4 to the 1982 Act. [PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.32] (2) The claimant may serve the claim form on a defendant in Scotland or Northern Ireland where each claim made against the defendant to be served and included in the claim form is a claim which the court has power to determine under any enactment other than the 1982 Act notwithstanding that –

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.32] (a) the person against whom the claim is made is not within the jurisdiction; or

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.32] (b) the facts giving rise to the claim did not occur within the jurisdiction. ## 6.33

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.33] (1) Omitted

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.33] (2) The claimant may serve the claim form on a defendant out of the United Kingdom where each claim made against the defendant to be served and included in the claim form is a claim which the court has power to determine under sections 15A to 15E of the 1982 Act and –

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.33] (a) No proceedings between the parties concerning the same claim are pending in the courts of any other part of the United Kingdom; and

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.33] (b)

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.33] (i) Omitted (ii) the defendant is not a consumer, but is a party to a consumer contract within section 15B(1) of the 1982 Act; or (iii) the defendant is an employer and a party to a contract of employment within section 15C(1) of the 1982 Act;

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.33] (2A) Omitted

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.33] 2B) The claimant may serve the claim form on a defendant outside the United Kingdom where, for each claim made against the defendant to be served and included in the claim form—

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.33] (a) the court has power to determine that claim under the 2005 Hague Convention and the defendant is a party to an exclusive choice of court agreement conferring jurisdiction on that court within the meaning of Article 3 of the 2005 Hague Convention;

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.33] (b) a contract contains a term to the effect that the court shall have jurisdiction to determine that claim; or

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.33] (c) the claim is in respect of a contract falling within sub-paragraph (b). [PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.33] (3) The claimant may serve the claim form on a defendant out of the United Kingdom where each claim made against the defendant to be served and included in the claim form is a claim which the court has power to determine other than under  the 2005 Hague Convention, notwithstanding that –

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.33] (a) the person against whom the claim is made is not within the jurisdiction; or

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.33] (b) the facts giving rise to the claim did not occur within the jurisdiction. ## Notice of statement of grounds where the permission of the court is not required for service

## 6.34

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.34] (1) Where the claimant intends to serve a claim form on a defendant under rule 6.32 or 6.33, the claimant must –

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.34] (a) file with the claim form a notice containing a statement of the grounds on which the claimant is entitled to serve the claim form out of the jurisdiction; and

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.34] (b) serve a copy of that notice with the claim form. [PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.34] (2) Where the claimant fails to file with the claim form a copy of the notice referred to in paragraph (1)(a), the claim form may only be served –

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.34] (a) once the claimant files the notice; or

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.34] (b) if the court gives permission. ## Period for responding to the claim form where permission was not required for service

## 6.35

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.35] (1) This rule sets out the period for –

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.35] (a) filing an acknowledgment of service;

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.35] (b) filing an admission; or

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.35] (c) filing a defence,

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.35] where a claim form has been served out of the jurisdiction under rule 6.32 or 6.33. [PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.35] (Part 10 contains rules about acknowledgments of service, Part 14 contains rules about admissions and Part 15 contains rules about defences.)

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.35] Service of the claim form on a defendant in Scotland or Northern Ireland

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.35] (2) Where the claimant serves on a defendant in Scotland or Northern Ireland under rule 6.32, the period –

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.35] (a) for filing an acknowledgment of service or admission is 21 days after service of the particulars of claim; or

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.35] (b) for filing a defence is –

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.35] (i) 21 days after service of the particulars of claim; or

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.35] (ii) where the defendant files an acknowledgment of service, 35 days after service of the particulars of claim. [PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.35] (Part 7 provides that particulars of claim must be contained in or served with the claim form or served separately on the defendant within 14 days after service of the claim form.)

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.35] Service on a defendant elsewhere

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.35] (5) Where the claimant serves the claim form under rule 6.33, the period for responding to the claim form is set out in Practice Direction 6B. ## Service of the claim form where the permission of the court is required

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > Service of the claim form where the permission of the court is required] 6.36 In any proceedings to which rule 6.32 or 6.33 does not apply, the claimant may serve a claim form out of the jurisdiction with the permission of the court if any of the grounds set out in paragraph 3.1 of Practice Direction 6B apply. ## Application for permission to serve the claim form out of the jurisdiction

## 6.37

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.37] (1) An application for permission under rule 6.36 must set out –

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.37] (a) which ground in paragraph 3.1 of Practice Direction 6B is relied on;

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.37] (b) that the claimant believes that the claim has a reasonable prospect of success; and

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.37] (c) the defendant’s address or, if not known, in what place the defendant is, or is likely, to be found. [PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.37] (2) Where the application is made in respect of a claim referred to in paragraph 3.1(3) of Practice Direction 6B, the application must also state the grounds on which the claimant believes that there is between the claimant and the defendant a real issue which it is reasonable for the court to try. [PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.37] (3) The court will not give permission unless satisfied that England and Wales is the proper place in which to bring the claim. [PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.37] (4) In particular, where –

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.37] (a) the application is for permission to serve a claim form in Scotland or Northern Ireland; and

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.37] (b) it appears to the court that the claimant may also be entitled to a remedy in Scotland or Northern Ireland, the court, in deciding whether to give permission, will –

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.37] (i) compare the cost and convenience of proceeding there or in the jurisdiction; and

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.37] (ii) (where relevant) have regard to the powers and jurisdiction of the Sheriff court in Scotland or the county courts or courts of summary jurisdiction in Northern Ireland. [PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.37] (5) Where the court gives permission to serve a claim form out of the jurisdiction –

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.37] (a) it will specify the periods within which the defendant may –

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.37] (i) file an acknowledgment of service;

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.37] (ii) file or serve an admission;

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.37] (iii) file a defence; or

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.37] (iv) file any other response or document required by a rule in another Part, any other enactment or a practice direction; and

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.37] (b) it may give directions about the method of service-

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.37] (i) give directions about the method of service; and

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.37] (ii) give permission for other documents in the proceedings to be served out of the jurisdiction. [PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.37] (The periods referred to in paragraphs (5)(a)(i), (ii) and (iii) are those specified in the Table in Practice Direction 6B.)

## Service of documents other than the claim form – permission

## 6.38

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.38] Any application notice issued or order made in any proceedings, or other document which is required to be served in the proceedings, may be served on a defendant out of the jurisdiction without permission where—

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.38] (a)the claim form has been served on the defendant out of the jurisdiction with permission; or

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.38] (b)permission is or was not required to serve the claim form (whether within or out of the jurisdiction). ## Service of application notice on a non-party to the proceedings

## 6.39

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.39] (1) Where an application notice is to be served out of the jurisdiction on a person who is not a party to the proceedings rules 6.35 and 6.37(5)(a)(i), (ii) and (iii) do not apply. [PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.39] (2) Where an application is served out of the jurisdiction on a person who is not a party to the proceedings, that person may make an application to the court under Part 11 as if that person were a defendant, but rule 11(2) does not apply. [PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.39] (Part 11 contains provisions about disputing the court’s jurisdiction.)

## Methods of service – general provisions

## 6.40

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.40] (1) This rule contains general provisions about the method of service of a claim form or other document on a party out of the jurisdiction. [PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.40] Where service is to be effected on a party in Scotland or Northern Ireland

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.40] (2) Where a party serves a claim form or other document on a party in Scotland or Northern Ireland, it must be served by a method permitted by Section II (and references to ‘jurisdiction’ in that Section are modified accordingly) or Section III of this Part and rule 6.23(4) applies. [PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.40] Where service is to be effected on a party out of the United Kingdom

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.40] (3) Where a party wishes to serve a claim form or other document on a party out of the United Kingdom, it may be served –

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.40] (a) by any method provided for by –

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.40] (i) Omitted

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.40] (ii) rule 6.42 (service through foreign governments, judicial authorities and British Consular authorities); or

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.40] (iii) rule 6.44 (service of claim form or other document on a State);

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.40] (b) by any method permitted by a Civil Procedure Convention or Treaty; or

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.40] (c) by any other method permitted by the law of the country in which it is to be served. [PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.40] (4) Nothing in paragraph (3) or in any court order authorises or requires any person to do anything which is contrary to the law of the country where the claim form or other document is to be served. [PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.40] (The texts of the Civil Procedure Treaties which the United Kingdom has entered into may be found on the Foreign and Commonwealth Office website at http://www.fco.gov.uk/en/publications-and-documents/treaties/lists-treaties/bilateral-civil-procedure.)

## 6.41

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.41] Omitted

## Service through foreign governments, judicial authorities and British Consular authorities

## 6.42

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.42] (1) Where a party wishes to serve a claim form or any other document in any country which is a party to a Civil Procedure Convention or Treaty providing for service in that country, it may be served –

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.42] (a) through the authority designated under the Hague Convention or any other Civil Procedure Convention or Treaty (where relevant) in respect of that country; or

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.42] (b) if the law of that country permits –

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.42] (i) through the judicial authorities of that country, or

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.42] (ii) through a British Consular authority in that country (subject to any provisions of the applicable convention about the nationality of persons who may be served by such a method). [PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.42] (2) Where a party wishes to serve a claim form or any other document in any country with respect to which there is no Civil Procedure Convention or Treaty providing for service in that country, the claim form or other document may be served, if the law of that country so permits –

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.42] (a) through the government of that country, where that government is willing to serve it; or

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.42] (b) through a British Consular authority in that country. [PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.42] (3) Where a party wishes to serve the claim form or other document in –

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.42] (a) any Commonwealth State which is not a party to the Hague Convention or is such a party but HM Government has not declared acceptance of its accession to the Convention;

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.42] (b) the Isle of Man or the Channel Islands; or
